scholarships.title: France 2030 - PEPR PROPSY – "Psychiatrie de précision" - Appel à projets - 2026
scholarships.official_source: Agence nationale de la recherche (ANR), France 2030 / PEPR PROPSY piloté par l'Inserm et le CNRS avec la Fondation FondaMental

eligibility: The submission file must be deposited complete on the ANR submission site before the closing date and time, and the administrative and financial document signed by each partner institution and scanned must be deposited at the date and time indicated in the call document.
The project scientific document must imperatively follow the template available on the call website and be deposited in unprotected PDF format.
Project duration must be 24-48 months for the pre-clinical axis and 36-48 months for the clinical and mixed axes.
Aid requested must be 500 000 €-800 000 € for the pre-clinical axis, 800 000 €-1 500 000 € for the clinical axis, and 800 000 €-2 000 000 € for the mixed axis.
The coordinating institution must be a French higher education and research institution, a research organisation, or a foundation of scientific cooperation.
For the clinical and mixed axes, projects are necessarily collaborative with a minimum of two different French research structures (structure identified by an RNSR number).

Beneficiaries are research organisations, higher education and research institutions, and recognised foundations of scientific cooperation described as "organismes de recherche et de diffusion des connaissances".

Private institutions contributing to public-service missions in higher education and research under article L.732-1 of the Code de l'Education may be financed after ANR analysis, MESRE opinion and SGPI validation.
Companies and foreign institutions may be associated as partners but cannot receive funding for that participation.
Pre-clinical studies may be single-team; collaborations are encouraged. Clinical and mixed projects must be collaborative.
Teams of the PROPSY "Projets Ciblés" are eligible as partners, but their coordinators are not authorised to coordinate a project in this call.
existing.eligibility_summary: A permanent researcher can lead a project on one of three axes, provided the coordinating institution is French, the duration and aid amount fall inside the axis-specific bands, the project targets the four PEPR PROPSY disorders, and clinical and mixed projects involve at least two different French research structures.
benefits: A grant (dotation) of between 500 000 € and 2 000 000 € per project depending on the axis, disbursed by the ANR to the coordinating institution according to the schedule set in the aid contract.
Indicative total envelope of about 9 600 000 € for this 2026 call, funding 8 to 16 projects; indicative per-axis envelopes of about 3 M€ (pre-clinical), 3.5 M€ (clinical) and 3.1 M€ (mixed).

Eligible expenditure is set by the PEPR financial regulation (Règlement financier des PEPR); the AAP states the aid may for example finance equipment purchases, personnel expenditure specifically assigned to the projects, and associated running costs.

Projects may build on existing national and international cohorts and databases, including the SNDS and the French Minds cohort, and the data sets mobilised must be identified and documented at submission to guarantee feasibility within the granted duration.

requirements: Open an account (login and password) on the ANR submission site in advance; the AAP recommends registering as early as possible.
Deposit the complete submission file electronically from the project manager's account before the published closing date and time.
Only the electronic version of the submission documents present on the submission site at the call closing time is taken into account for evaluation.
Contribute to strengthening and enhancing the capacity of French research actors, their attractiveness, their European and international influence, and their impact on the economy and society.
Produce high-quality research strengthening the acquisition of disciplinary and/or interdisciplinary scientific knowledge to address current and future precision-psychiatry issues.
Valorise the research and innovation produced, accompanying clinical implementation and/or industrialisation.
Integrate the sharing of data, results and knowledge in an open science logic.

Respect the PROPSY thematic scope: projects mainly on addictions are not eligible, except where those conditions are addressed within precision psychiatry as secondary phenomena or comorbidities of one of the four PEPR PROPSY disorders.

Integrate a humanities and social sciences dimension where relevant, for example analysis of care pathways, clinical, social or ethical acceptability of innovations, and/or the involvement of patients, affected persons or associations in the design, implementation and valorization of projects.
Signal any overlap with an already funded or submitted project and supply, where applicable, the justifications showing the absence of duplication.
Where relevant, rely on public or private co-funding, national or international: these are not mandatory but are encouraged.

For clinical studies, the data sets mobilised (cohorts, national or international databases, SNDS or existing health data warehouse data) must be identified and documented from the submission to guarantee project feasibility within the granted duration.

For clinical studies, included patients must present at least one disorder of interest to PEPR PROPSY (bipolar disorders, resistant depressions, psychotic disorders, autism spectrum disorders) and/or the project may cover several disorders simultaneously.

For the pre-clinical axis, explicitly declare the co-deposit of the project or obtain agreement from the French and foreign partner institutions; the actual co-deposit wording is not published in the AAP for this axis, so confirm it with the ANR contact.
documents: Scientific document (document scientifique): maximum 15 pages, written in English, describing the proposed project following the published template, with in appendix the list of scientific publications of the last three years of the researchers/teams proposing the project.

Administrative and financial document (document administratif et financier): Excel format, covering the administrative and budget description of the project, with the commitment letters of the partner institutions integrated.

Trame document scientifique (scientific document template, .docx), Trame de l'annexe publication (publications annex template, .docx) and Trame du document administratif et financier (administrative and financial template, .xlsx) supplied by the ANR.
Data Management Plan (Plan de Gestion de Données, PGD): first version within the 6 months following project start, per the ANR modalities.
Consortium agreement (accord de consortium) where required - mandatory when companies are involved, otherwise within 12 months of contract signature when exigé.
existing.english_requirement: The scientific document must be written in English (rédigé en anglais), maximum 15 pages, using the published template and deposited as an unprotected PDF. No English requirement is published for the administrative and financial document or for the interview language.
application_method: Open an account on the ANR submission site as early as possible.
Download the Word scientific document template, the Word publications annex template and the Excel administrative and financial template from the call page.

Draft the scientific document in English, 15 pages maximum, on the template, including the three-year publication list appendix, the axis chosen, the duration, the data sets mobilised and the co-funding declared.
Complete the administrative and financial Excel document, with the aid amount inside the band for the chosen axis.
Obtain the signed commitment letters of all partner institutions and the legal representative signature on the administrative and financial document, then scan them as required.
Upload the documents into the 'documents de dépôt' and 'documents signés' sections of the call entry on the submission site.
Validate the deposit electronically before 10/11/2026 at 11:00 CET and keep the electronic acknowledgement of receipt.
Optionally contact the PEPR PROPSY direction team at aap@pepr-propsy.fr before submitting, to check that the topic and project structure fit the call.
existing.selection_notes: Only proposals meeting the eligibility criteria (critères de recevabilité) are transmitted to the evaluation committee and can in no case be funded. Eligible projects are evaluated by an independent international-dimension committee, which may use external experts and may hear project leaders (with project representatives) after transmitting questions in advance. The committee delivers to the PEPR PROPSY scientific directors a report with a list of projects recommended for funding, a list of projects it proposes not to fund for insufficient quality on at least one criterion, a written justification for every project, and possibly an opinion on the amounts requested. The PEPR PROPSY scientific directors then propose to the SGPI which projects could be financed and at what amount; the Prime Minister, after SGPI opinion, decides beneficiaries and amounts, and each project is covered by a contract between the ANR and the coordinating institution. Evaluation criteria fall into three groups: (1) excellence and scientific ambition in precision psychiatry - clarity of objectives and hypotheses, innovativeness, ambition, originality, methodological or conceptual rupture against the state of the art, methodological relevance, preliminary data, project feasibility; (2) quality of the consortium, project management, resources mobilised and governance - competence, expertise and involvement of the project leader including capacity to coordinate ambitious multidisciplinary projects or consortia, academic track record, international recognition, quality and complementarity of the scientific consortium, adequacy between human and financial means and the objectives, relevance of the schedule and management of scientific risks with alternative solutions and credible milestones, relevance and efficiency of governance including patient associations and links with industrial partners or other programmes; (3) impact and outcomes - capacity to address precision-psychiatry development issues, active strategy to measure economic and/or societal impact, contribution to solutions for pathophysiological, diagnostic or therapeutic issues, dissemination and valorization strategy in itinere and ex post, adherence to FAIR and Open Science principles and promotion of scientific culture. Committee members and external experts commit to ANR deontology and integrity rules, strict confidentiality, declaration of conflicts of interest, and a ban on AI tools in the evaluation.
existing.best_fit: A permanent researcher at a French research organisation, higher education and research institution, or recognised foundation of scientific cooperation, who can coordinate a 24-48 month precision-psychiatry project of 500 000 € to 2 M€ and, for the clinical and mixed axes, assemble a consortium of at least two different French research structures.
existing.notes: Aid is a one-off exceptional allocation, distinct from recurrent institutional funding, intended for new actions, paid as a grant (dotation) to the coordinating institution. It is institutional research funding, not a personal scholarship: nothing is paid to individual students, and tuition, living costs or individual travel allowances are not covered. Consortiums without companies are not obliged to conclude and transmit a consortium agreement; where it is required (mandatory when companies are involved, otherwise when exigé), the coordinating institution must supply it to the ANR within a maximum of 12 months of contract signature, and its absence can lead to cessation of funding and repayment under article 6.6 of the Financial Regulation. Beneficiaries must guarantee immediate open access to peer-reviewed publications under CC-BY, deposit the accepted manuscript or publisher version in HAL, deliver a first PGD within 6 months of project start, deposit data in a reference thematic repository or recherche.data.gouv, and must mention the France 2030 support with the Plan France 2030 and PEPR PROPSY logos in communications. Funded projects must send accepted publications to the PEPR PROPSY direction team for diffusion and archiving, and annual indicator reporting to the State and the ANR is required. Financial aid may constitute State aid under TFEU Article 107(1) and is subject to the French research State-aid framework 2022/C 414/01, the RDI exemption regime SA.111723, the de-minimis Regulation 2023/2831 and the 2011/20/EU decision. Projects mainly on addictions are out of scope unless addictions appear as secondary phenomena or comorbidities of one of the four targeted disorders.
